title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
abstract: Modeling gene regulation in single cells requires jointly representing DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression across regulatory scales. Sequence-based models capture DNA-level regulatory grammar but often lack cell-level resolution, whereas many single-cell omics models represent genes and peaks as fixed-vocabulary tokens without their underlying sequence. Here, we present MUSS, a sequence-based multi-scale model for single-cell gene regulation that preserves both DNA-level and cell-level resolution. MUSS derives peak- and gene-level representations from DNA using a frozen pre-trained sequence encoder and integrates them through peak-peak self-attention and distance-biased peak-gene interactions. Peak masked language modeling followed by training on paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq aligns these representations with cell-specific regulatory states. Across gene expression prediction, enhancer-gene linking, motif-guided regulatory prioritization, and zero-shot cell clustering, MUSS achieves strong performance against sequence-based and single-cell omics baselines. It further predicts expression for genes and peaks unseen during task training. These results support sequence-grounded, multi-scale representations for decoding cell-type-specific regulatory programs. Code, datasets, and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/MUSS_neurips26.

_summary.task_scope: 输入：DNA序列、配对的scATAC-seq与scRNA-seq数据 → 输出：基因表达预测、增强子-基因关联、调控优先级排序及零样本细胞聚类；研究物种/细胞体系：摘要未说明；验证范围：基于单细胞多组学数据，涵盖多种细胞类型（含零样本聚类验证）
_summary.core_method: 基于冻结的预训练序列编码器提取peak与基因特征，结合距离偏置的注意力机制与掩码语言建模，在多组学数据上对齐细胞特异性调控状态。
_summary.main_finding: MUSS在基因表达预测、增强子-基因关联等任务上优于序列和单细胞组学基线，并能泛化预测训练时未见的基因和peak；摘要未提供具体性能指标数字。

title: A framework for genome-wide characterization of DNA methylation and variant effect prediction.
abstract: DNA methylation plays a critical role in many essential biological processes, including transcriptional regulation, genomic imprinting, chromosomal maintenance, genomic stability and development, and has phenotypic and disease impacts. However, genome-wide characterization of methylation patterns across cell types and tissues remains a major challenge. Here, to address this, we present a framework that enables systematic genome-wide analysis of methylation and sequence-based prediction of context-specific methylation effects of variants. Our data-driven discovery of methylation classes reveals context-dependent roles for methylation across tissues, cell types and regions of the genome. The framework also includes Wreath, a deep learning-based sequence model specifically designed to accurately predict the context-dependent impact of any genetic variant on methylation. These developments leverage a compendium that harmonizes disparate methylation profiles from disparate studies including over 90 tissues and cell types. Using Wreath, we systematically characterized the impact of noncoding pathogenic variants on tissue-specific methylation, generating mechanistic hypotheses for individual regulatory variants. We make the full framework, including the compendium, the methylation classes and the model, available for use by the community.
corr_affiliation: Flatiron Institute of the Simons Foundation, New York, NY, USA. ogt@princeton.edu.

title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
abstract: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%. Relative to gene-wise reasoning on matched drug-cell cohorts, measured language-model token use falls by 99.77% for Predict and 98.41% for Explain. On the source-grounded benchmark, Explain correctly answers all answerable questions with supporting proofs and identifies all insufficient-evidence cases. In simulated experimental feedback, Update uses one measured source context per drug to exceed the best fine-tuned baselines in differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 without changing model weights. Together, these capabilities support a cumulative account of cellular responses, with predictions and biological judgments that can be revised as evidence accumulates.
